newsitem.title: USA: Democrats pressured Clinton on fund-raising calls.
newsitem.headline: Democrats pressured Clinton on fund-raising calls.

text.p: The pressure to raise money for President Clinton's re-election grew so great in late 1995 that the Democratic Party pressed the president and Vice President Al Gore to telephone donors directly, according to documents released by the White House Wednesday.

The documents, which belong to former White House Deputy Chief of Staff Harold Ickes, included a memo from top party officials arguing that such calls and a string of fund-raising events were needed to raise $3.2 million for paid television advertising. Clinton has said he does not recall making such phone calls, although he cannot rule it out, while Gore has said he made "a few" fund-raising calls from the White House.

"Because of the short lead time and lack of time to cultivate additional donors, we believe the following represents the maximum that can be raised prior to year end," said a memo dated Nov. 20, 1995 from four top Democratic Party officials to Ickes.

The memo then listed a series of proposed activities by the president, referred to by his White House acronym POTUS, or President of the United States, and the vice president, who is listed as VPOTUS.

These included "18-20 calls by POTUS" and "10 calls by VPOTUS" as well as a lunch and dinner attended by Clinton, two unspecified events attended by Gore, two by first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton and an unspecified "White House Dinner" adding up to $3.2 million for the re-election effort.

A second memo dated Nov. 28, 1995 from Ickes to Clinton and Gore raises the ante, saying that Marvin Rosen, a top party fund-raiser, believed that a greater effort would be required, including about 20 phone calls by Clinton, 15 by Gore and 10 by the first lady.
